title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling policies will cover legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt files (Worldwide)
summary: Hold for one incorrect comparison of the rollout dates. The notice targets preview completion in early December, so not all its preview dates fall within the roadmap's November preview target month; the detailed schedule, controls and licensing are otherwise supported.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy reaches policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select your policy to see the details of the configuration and status. When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -Mode Enable enables the identified policy.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the policy. Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: TestWithoutNotifications keeps an auto-labeling policy in test mode.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations where you want to apply the label reaches location selection.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies ... select the Edit policy option ... For the page Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation <SharePointSiteLocation> adds a SharePoint site location to the policy.
claims.quote: The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the SharePointLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: AddOneDriveLocation is the parameter for adding OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy opens the policy editor.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select your policy to see the details of the configuration and status. For a policy in the Off section, select the Edit policy button.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -Comment <text> edits the identified policy's comment.
claims.quote: The Comment parameter specifies an optional comment. If you specify a value that contains spaces, enclose the value in quotation marks ("). The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether a PowerShell Comment edit restarts the legacy-format crawl in the same way as the notice's portal edit and rerun.
claims.quote: Searched: "legacy" "auto-labeling" "Comment" crawl PowerShell; read MC1530948, auto-labeling Learn and Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy. StartSimulation restarts simulation generally; no text links Comment or that parameter to the legacy-format crawl.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity turns auditing on when it is disabled.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity. Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns auditing on.
claims.quote: Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Turning auditing on requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: The auditing command runs in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Complete the following steps to turn on auditing by using Exchange Online PowerShell: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The change is admin-opt-in for extending existing policies; new policies include the formats when an administrator creates them.
claims.quote: New auto-labeling policies will automatically support these file formats. Existing auto-labeling policies require a small policy edit and another policy run to restart the crawl and evaluate legacy Office files.

claims.where: Governance controls: applicability and portal management
claims.claim: Administrators govern the legacy-format capability through the existing Purview auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: Admins manage the capability through Microsoft Purview auto-labeling policies. Microsoft Learn identifies the Microsoft Purview portal's Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies surface for service-side auto-labeling.

claims.claim: The notice identifies organizations using service-side auto-labeling for SharePoint and OneDrive files as affected and does not identify Exchange.
claims.quote: Who is affected: Organizations using Microsoft Purview service-side auto-labeling policies for files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Administrators can inspect matching documents in Items to review before turning the policy on.
claims.quote: For policies in simulation mode, select the Items to review tab to see which emails or documents matched the rules that you specified. When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Before enabling a new or updated policy, run it in simulation mode and review the results to confirm that it identifies the intended content.

claims.claim: The Choose locations where you want to apply the label page lets administrators select and specify SharePoint and OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: For the page Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.
